what: RenaissanceRe is a reinsurer: it insures insurance companies against the biggest losses, particularly hurricanes, earthquakes and other catastrophes, and it also manages capital for outside investors who want that risk.
customers: Primary insurers worldwide buying protection against the losses that would otherwise break them.
money: catastrophe reinsurance, the business it is known for
liability, marine, credit and other lines
managing third-party capital in its funds
moat: Decades of catastrophe modelling and the capital to write the largest risks, in a market where only a handful of firms can take a meaningful share of a hurricane.
risks: One severe hurricane season can erase a year of profit
Reinsurance prices move in cycles, and after several profitable years prices usually soften
Results swing far more year to year than almost any other financial business
opportunities: 9.6 times earnings and 4.9 times free cash flow after revenue grew from $5.1B to $12.8B in three years
A 20.9% net margin in a hard market where reinsurance prices rose sharply
Fee income from managing other people's catastrophe capital grows without risking its own
watch: Reinsurance renewal pricing each January, and the combined ratio.
